key_insight: An In2S3/Cu2NiGeS4/MoTe2 thin-film solar-cell stack is computationally shown to enable strong carrier selectivity and a highly optimized photovoltaic response, reaching 28.44% simulated efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a device-level design blueprint for improving quaternary chalcogenide photovoltaics through absorber, interface, and transport-layer engineering.
method: SCAPS-1D simulation of the full heterostructure
Band, electric-field, carrier, and recombination analysis
Parameter sweeps for thickness, doping, defects, resistances, temperature, and illumination
evidence_signal: Under AM1.5G illumination at 300 K, the optimized device is predicted to deliver 0.984 V Voc, 34.39 mA/cm² Jsc, 84.04% FF, and 28.44% PCE, outperforming previously reported CNGS ranges cited in the abstract.
watch_item: The result is simulation-based, so real-device performance may be limited by fabrication quality, interface defects, and material stability not fully captured in the model.
paper_title: Device Engineering and Performance Optimization of Cu2NiGeS4 Thin-Film Solar Cells with In2S3/MoTe2 Charge-Selective Layers: A Computational Study
